title: The Crucifixion Question
subtitle: The historical case, the Quranic denial, and why Muslims trust revelation
summary: The earliest Christian sources present Jesus as crucified, and most historians accept that a crucifixion occurred. The Quran nevertheless states that Jesus was neither killed nor crucified, but that it was made to appear so, and that God raised him. Islam does not deny the evidence carelessly; it distinguishes what historical methods can infer from surviving reports from what reliable revelation can disclose about an exceptional event.

seo.metaTitle: The Crucifixion Question: Islam, Christianity, and History
seo.metaDescription: The early crucifixion evidence, the Quran's different claim, and the positive reasons needed to trust a corrective revelation.
keywords: did Jesus die on the cross

sections.title: Why Muslims Reject the Crucifixion of Jesus
sections.body: Most historians accept a crucifixion because Paul's letters and the Gospels are early sources that say it occurred. Muslims acknowledge that evidence while trusting the Quran's explicit correction: Jesus was not killed or crucified, and God raised him. The real issue is therefore whether the Quran is revelation and can correct a conclusion based on human testimony.

sections.title: The Historical Objection Must Be Faced
sections.body:
Jesus's crucifixion is not a late marginal claim within Christianity. Paul speaks of his death, and all four canonical Gospels narrate it. Most historians accept a Roman execution, including many who do not accept Christian theology.

Islam nevertheless follows Quran 4:157-158. The difficult question is why a later claim of revelation should outweigh the earlier surviving record. Small Gospel differences do not settle it. Begin with [Why the Quran?](/articles/why-the-quran) if that authority has not yet been examined.

sections.title: Historical Probability and Revealed Authority
sections.body:
Historical study asks what explanation best accounts for surviving evidence. It need not assume the New Testament is inspired to judge that Jesus was crucified. An ordinary execution and a supernatural resurrection are also different claims with different evidential burdens; they should not be treated as equally unavailable to historians.

Islam makes a further theological claim: God revealed a correction to what people believed had happened. That is coherent for someone with independent reasons to trust the Quran, but the possibility of divine intervention is not itself evidence that an intervention occurred.

sections.title: What the Early Christian Evidence Establishes
sections.body:
In [1 Corinthians 15:3-4](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/1corinthians/15), Paul says he passed on what he received about Christ's death, burial, and resurrection. The Gospels narrate a crucifixion as well. Their shared central claim cannot be removed by pointing to differences in surrounding details.

These sources establish early Christian conviction and form a major part of historians' case for an actual execution. A historical reconstruction is not infallible, but calling its evidence human testimony does not make it worthless.

sections.title: The Quran's Clear Correction
sections.body:
The Quran states:

وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ لَفِى شَكٍّۢ مِّنْهُ ۚ مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ ۚ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًۢا

'They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but it was made to appear so to them ... They did not kill him for certain' (Quran 4:157). The next verse says:

بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًۭا

'Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise' (Quran 4:158).

The Quran does not name another person, describe the precise mechanism, or authorize certainty about details it leaves unstated. Its central affirmations are clear: Jesus's enemies did not succeed, and God raised His messenger.

sections.title: What the New Testament Affirms
sections.body: The Gospels narrate Jesus's arrest, trial, crucifixion, burial, and appearances after death. Paul writes that Christ died and was raised (1 Corinthians 15:3–4). Christians interpret these claims as the saving center of the Gospel. The accounts also contain differences in chronology and detail, but the broad crucifixion claim is common to them and should not be hidden.

sections.title: Why Trust the Quran's Correction?
sections.body:
Why prefer the Quran's later account over earlier Christian testimony? Saying only that the Quran claims divine authority would assume the answer.

The positive Islamic case begins with an independently meaningful account of God: the self-sufficient Creator need not become a dependent creature, and He can forgive responsible people without requiring an innocent person's death. The Quran consistently presents Jesus within that Creator-messenger distinction. This gives the Muslim reading explanatory coherence, not merely a denial of the cross.

Muhammad's credibility also has concrete evidence to examine. [Sahih al-Bukhari 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043) reports that people connected an eclipse with his son Ibrahim's death, but he rejected that flattering interpretation rather than exploit it. As transmitted character evidence, this supports the Muslim assessment of his truthfulness if the report is credible; it is not independent proof that every religious claim is true. [Who Is Prophet Muhammad?](/articles/who-is-prophet-muhammad) develops the wider inquiry.

These considerations begin a case for trusting the message; they do not by themselves disprove crucifixion. A divine correction takes priority only if the revelation's credentials are established. For a reader not yet persuaded of those credentials, the strong historical objection remains unresolved.

sections.title: No Invented Substitute and No Claimed Knowledge of God's Hidden Purpose
sections.body:
The Quran does not name a substitute or explain the precise mechanism behind what appeared to people. It gives no detailed story about who stood where or why particular observers believed what they did.

A Christian can also ask why God would allow a mistaken account to become so widespread. These verses do not disclose a full purpose. Human misunderstanding is not the same as a divine command to adopt false belief, but that distinction does not fill every gap. Nor does rescuing Jesus imply that God never allowed another prophet to be killed.

sections.title: Forgiveness Does Not Depend on an Innocent Person's Death
sections.body:
Quran 35:18 grounds personal responsibility: no soul carries another's burden. Islam joins responsibility to repentance and divine mercy, without requiring Jesus's death to make forgiveness possible.

Christians understand the cross as the Son's willing saving act, not simply the punishment of an unwilling outsider. Islam rejects the underlying incarnation and atonement account, while offering a positive alternative: answer for your own choices, repair harm where you can, and seek mercy directly from God.

sections.title: Investigate the Authority That Carries the Claim
sections.body:
The Muslim conclusion is firm as a matter of faith: God raised Jesus, and his enemies did not kill or crucify him as they claimed. The historical objection remains serious and must not be relabeled as proof for Islam.

Read [The Crucifixion and History](/articles/the-crucifixion-and-history) for the evidence, then [Why the Quran?](/articles/why-the-quran) for the source of the proposed correction. For the personal question of forgiveness, continue to [Forgiveness in Islam and Christianity](/articles/forgiveness-in-islam-and-christianity).

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Do Muslims believe Jesus was crucified?
A: No. Quran 4:157 states that Jesus was neither killed nor crucified and 4:158 states that God raised him.

Q: If it was not Jesus on the cross, who was it?
A: The Quran does not identify another person. Specific substitute stories are interpretations, not explicit Quranic teaching.

Q: Don't historians agree the crucifixion happened?
A: Yes. Most historians accept a Roman crucifixion from the surviving evidence without needing to accept Christian theology. Islam's disagreement rests on trusting Quran 4:157-158 as revelation, not on claiming historical method has disproved the event.

Q: Without the cross, how are sins forgiven in Islam?
A: Through sincere repentance, responsibility for one's conduct, and God's mercy. Quran 35:18 rejects transferring another person's moral burden. Christians have several accounts of atonement; Islam's alternative does not require an innocent person's death before God can forgive.

Q: Is Jesus alive now, according to Islam?
A: Islam teaches that God raised Jesus and that he will return before the end of time. Details are established from authentic revelation, not speculation.

Q: Does denying the crucifixion dishonor Jesus?
A: Islam understands the raising of Jesus as God's vindication. Christians instead see the cross as willing sacrifice and subsequent victory, not dishonor. The disagreement concerns what happened and how salvation works, not whether either tradition intends to demean Jesus.

sections.title: Further Reading
sections.body:
Selected sources and further reading:

- **The Crucifixion and the Qur'an: A Study in the History of Muslim Thought** — Todd Lawson. A scholarly survey of how Muslim commentators across the centuries have interpreted Quran 4:157, showing the range of readings from substitution to appearance.
- **Christ in Islam and Christianity** — Neal Robinson. A careful academic comparison of the Jesus of the Quran and classical Muslim exegesis with the Jesus of Christian doctrine, including the crucifixion passages.
- **Jesus in the Qur'an** — Geoffrey Parrinder. A classic, sympathetic study of every Quranic passage about Jesus, written by a scholar of comparative religion and accessible to beginners.
- **The Muslim Jesus: Sayings and Stories in Islamic Literature** — Tarif Khalidi. A collection showing the deep reverence for Jesus within the Islamic tradition beyond the Quran itself.
- **Jesus: Apocalyptic Prophet of the New Millennium** — Bart D. Ehrman. A reconstruction of the historical Jesus by a prominent non-Christian historian — useful for seeing how the secular historical case for the crucifixion is actually argued.

quranVerses.arabic: وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا ٱلْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ لَفِى شَكٍّۢ مِّنْهُ ۚ مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ ۚ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًۢا
quranVerses.translation: And [for] their saying, "Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًۭا
quranVerses.translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِۦ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِۦ ۖ وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًۭا
quranVerses.translation: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَىٰٓ إِنِّى مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَىَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَجَاعِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ۖ ثُمَّ إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ فِيمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
quranVerses.translation: [Mention] when Allah said, "O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you [in submission to Allah alone] superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ ۚ وَإِن تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا لَا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌۭ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰٓ ۗ إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَأَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ ۚ وَمَن تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
quranVerses.translation: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to [carry some of] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and have established prayer. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for [the benefit of] his soul. And to Allah is the [final] destination.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
It was the third hour, and they crucified him.
About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible to you. Please remove this cup from me. However, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
